Data handling

Privacy notice

Effective November 2, 2026.

PROCURATOR is operated by the owner for personal administrative use. This notice describes the current deployed assistant and these public information pages.

Information the assistant accesses

With the owner’s Google authorization, the assistant can access Gmail message metadata and content; Drive file names, identifiers and metadata; and Google Docs content needed for requested tasks. It also processes the owner’s Telegram instructions and replies, generated summaries, document text and task results. After a separate iCloud connection, it can also access selected iCloud inbox headers and bounded message excerpts, and save requested draft copies in the account’s Drafts folder. Its server stores Google authorization credentials and, if connected, an Apple app-specific password to maintain access.

How information is used

Google data is used to perform the owner’s requested tasks, such as summarizing selected email, answering a question about a document or preparing a new Google Doc. The assistant reads Gmail and can request additional authorization to send Gmail messages. Each outgoing email requires an exact-content preview and a separate command from the authenticated owner in Telegram. Private assistant drafts contain the complete sender, recipients (including Cc and Bcc), subject and body. Supported Drive writes are limited by its tools to the designated assistant workspace.

This app does not sell Google user data, use it for advertising or use it to train generalized AI models. Its use and transfer of Google API data follows the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

Browser tasks

For requested browsing, Browserbase hosts a separate cloud browser that processes the selected websites, page contents and form entries. Selected page text and form controls are passed to Anthropic so the assistant can plan steps. Routine entries, exact page navigation and specific dropdown choices can run within a bounded task scope approved by the authenticated owner in Telegram. Final submissions, consent and other unrecognized actions still require a separate literal action review and owner command. Task state and continuation receipts are retained privately; a queued wake request does not establish task completion. Some websites transmit fields as they are typed. Credentials, verification codes, identity numbers and payment details should be entered and completed directly by the owner through browser takeover. The first browser version uses fresh sessions without saved login contexts or automated document uploads.

Realtime voice, when configured

Realtime phone mode sends live call audio and the owner-approved call brief to OpenAI, alongside Twilio telephony. Anthropic continues to process private text call summaries. Telegram receives the owner’s reviews and reports. Audio recording remains disabled. The approval review identifies the voice processors, and changing voice mode invalidates pending approvals. Realtime voice is activated only after a separate private API connection is configured.

Services that process information

  • Google: provides Gmail, Drive and Docs access and stores documents created in the connected account. A dedicated Google Cloud VM also processes approved iCloud messages and the app-specific password in memory to authenticate to Apple’s mail server. The relay’s application journal stores send identifiers, content hashes, recipients and outcomes; it does not store message bodies or the Apple password.
  • Apple: provides connected iCloud inbox access. Approved iCloud messages are sent to Apple through a dedicated Google Cloud relay.
  • Browserbase: runs cloud browser sessions for requested website tasks. The application disables recording and session logging for ordinary sessions; synthetic practice sessions can be recorded for testing. Browserbase still processes session data under its own policies.
  • DuckDuckGo and visited websites: receive public search queries or page requests needed for requested research.
  • Anthropic: receives selected task instructions, website text and form controls, and Google and connected iCloud content through its API to generate the assistant’s responses and drafts.
  • Telegram: carries the owner’s bot messages and the assistant’s replies. Replies can contain summaries or other content derived from Google data.
  • DigitalOcean: hosts the assistant server, including conversation history, task records and credentials.

These services apply their own account terms and data practices. Processing occurs when needed for the owner’s tasks; this notice does not make separate promises about each provider’s retention or internal operations.

Restricted phone tests

During owner-controlled phone connection tests, Twilio processes phone numbers, speech audio for recognition, and generated speech. Text from the call is sent to the existing Anthropic API to generate replies. Audio recording is disabled. The phone agent uses a separate workspace and has no ordinary assistant tools or private email, Drive or owner-memory access. Incoming tests are limited by caller-number filtering, which is not strong identity authentication. Outgoing tests require a separate authenticated Telegram owner approval. Calls are limited to one minute.

Storage and retention

The server retains conversation and task state, action identifiers and output links. A private browser database stores session identifiers, exact reviewed action plans, visible form values and action results. It is protected by server permissions, is not application-encrypted and has no automatic deletion schedule. The Browserbase API key is stored in a separate root-private file. The owner can revoke it in Browserbase settings. Google authorization credentials are held in a private file-backed keyring. Email drafts, approval timestamps, exact outgoing MIME snapshots and send receipts are retained in a private server database. If iCloud is connected, its app-specific password is stored in a private server file. These files are restricted by server permissions; the private mail database and iCloud credential file are not application-encrypted. Drafts and send records have no automatic deletion schedule in this version. Google Drive retains created files, and Telegram retains messages according to the respective account settings and provider behavior.

Revoking authorization stops future Google API access but does not automatically erase existing server history, Telegram messages or generated Google Drive files. The owner can delete outputs in Drive and Telegram and contact the app operator to remove retained assistant records and credentials from the server.

Owner controls

The owner can stop using the bot, request removal of the server’s stored connection or revoke Google access through Google Account connections. The owner can revoke an iCloud app-specific password through Apple Account settings. Revocation stops future iCloud access but does not erase retained drafts or history. Removing account access may prevent pending tasks from completing. Contact owner@example.com about access, deletion or privacy questions.

Public information pages

These pages have no analytics, advertising, forms or cookies. They do not display Gmail content, private documents or authorization credentials. Hosting and server error logs may contain technical connection details needed to operate the site.

Changes

This notice will be updated when the assistant’s features or data handling change. Gmail sending is available only after the owner grants the additional permission and approves each exact email in Telegram. iCloud sending uses a separately configured relay and requires exact-content Telegram approval for every email. Phone support includes incoming message-taking and short, individually approved outgoing assignments. Callers are told they are speaking to an AI assistant and that speech is transcribed and summarized privately for the owner. Twilio processes speech; Anthropic receives the call brief and text needed for conversation and summaries; Telegram receives private owner reports. Audio recording is disabled. Call metadata, text transcripts, pending reviews and attempt receipts are retained in private server state with no automatic deletion schedule. Twilio credentials are kept in private server files and made available to the gateway runtime; these files are not application-encrypted. Provider-side processing and retention follow the respective provider terms. The phone agent has no email, Drive, browser or owner-memory access. Only an active session-bound approved brief supplies outbound task facts. Call reports may contain caller statements that have not been independently verified. Reception admission metadata (call identifiers, hashed caller numbers, daily admission decisions) is kept in a private local database for up to seven prior UTC days, pruned when subsequent calls are admitted.
